name: Mandazi
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, cardamom and salt so the raising agent is evenly distributed. Pour in the coconut milk and mix to a soft dough.
Knead briefly until smooth, adding only a dusting of flour if very sticky. Cover and rest for 30 minutes; this makes the dough easier to roll without toughening it.
Roll the dough to about 8 mm thick. Cut into squares, then diagonally into roughly 16 triangles; keep the pieces covered while the oil heats.
Heat the oil in a deep pan to about 170°C. Fry a few triangles at a time for 2–3 minutes per side, turning once, until puffed and evenly golden with no raw centre.
Lift out and drain on a rack or paper. Serve warm; split one to check its breadlike crumb before serving the whole batch.
tips: Keep the oil moderately hot: very hot oil browns the outside before the centre cooks.
passiveTime: Rest the kneaded dough for 30 minutes.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
